answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed homing-pigeon loft beside a named willow, its birds ringed by the racing federation and logged in public race records; the loft's call sign is a sonnet read aloud at every race start. Random checks summon the holder to release that exact bird from the loft within hours, and one keeper cannot fly two lofts at once. The loft fee in outside money doubles per further loft on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real loft, another flock, another human, and twice the prior fee, driving a farm's budget toward its nadir.
